title: Poulet au Vinaigre
description: Chicken browned in butter and simmered in a sharp sauce of wine vinegar, shallots and tomato, rounded off with cream. It became a speciality of Lyon's cooking in the 20th century, and Paul Bocuse, whose restaurant at Collonges-au-Mont-d'Or held three Michelin stars from 1965, did much to make it famous.
notes:
Inspired by Paul Bocuse, *Paul Bocuse's French Cooking* (1977). Written for Sous; not his recipe.

The vinegar is the whole point, so use a good aged red wine vinegar; sherry vinegar also works. Taste the finished sauce: if it is too sharp, add a spoonful more cream; if it tastes flat, add a few drops of vinegar.

The dish reheats well. Keep the sauce and chicken together and warm gently, covered, so the sauce does not split.
ingredients: 1 chicken (3 1/2 to 4 pounds / 1.6 to 1.8 kg), cut into 8 pieces, or 3 pounds (1.4 kg) bone-in, skin-on thighs and drumsticks
1 tablespoon unsalted butter, plus 2 tablespoons cold butter to finish
2 ripe tomatoes, peeled, seeded and chopped, or 1 tablespoon tomato paste
1/3 cup (80 ml) crème fraîche or heavy cream
Rice or boiled potatoes, for serving
steps: Pat the chicken dry and season all over with the salt and pepper. If you have time, leave it uncovered in the fridge for an hour or up to a day.

Heat the oil and 1 tablespoon butter in a wide, lidded sauté pan over medium heat. Lay the chicken in skin side down and cook, without moving, until the skin is deep golden, 8 to 10 minutes. Turn and cook 3 minutes more, then move to a plate.
Pour off all but about 1 tablespoon of fat. Add the shallots and cook, stirring, until soft, about 2 minutes, then add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Pour in the vinegar (stand back from the sharp steam) and boil, scraping the pan, until reduced by about half, 3 to 4 minutes. Add the wine, stock and tomatoes and bring to a simmer.

Return the legs and thighs to the pan skin side up, keeping the skin above the liquid. Cover and simmer gently for 15 minutes. Tuck in the breast pieces, if using, and simmer, covered, until the breast reads 160°F (71°C) and the thighs at least 175°F (79°C), 15 to 20 minutes more.
Move the chicken to a warm platter. Boil the sauce until reduced to about 1 cup and lightly syrupy, 5 to 8 minutes.
Lower the heat and whisk in the cream; simmer for 1 minute. Take the pan off the heat and whisk in the cold butter a piece at a time until glossy. Stir in the tarragon and season.
Pour the sauce around the chicken, not over the skin, and serve with rice or potatoes.
